messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph during school hours. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Stop Signs & Traffic Signals** | • Must come to a complete stop at stop signs.
• Red lights mean stop; green means go (unless a sign says otherwise). | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on freeways unless overtaking. | | **Headlights** | • Must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for parking violations or if they pose a hazard. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks. | | **School Bus** | • Stop when a school bus stops with its red lights flashing. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display registration stickers.
• Proof of insurance is required. | | **Traffic Violations & Penalties** | • Fines vary by offense; points added to driver’s record.
• Accumulating points can lead to license suspension. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1) – the statutory source. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website – provides forms, guidelines, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement and public safety resources. If you need more specific details (e.g., statutes, recent amendments, or how to contest a ticket), let me know!
